questions.question:
Directions: Select the word that is most SIMILAR in meaning to the word given in the sentence-

To __digress__ for a moment, I would like to remind you that there will be no classes next week.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**deviate"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To **digress** means to stray from the main topic or subject being discussed or written about. It can also refer to moving away from the main point or purpose. (विषयांतर करने का अर्थ है चर्चा या लिखे जाने वाले मुख्य विषय से भटक जाना। इसका अर्थ मुख्य बिंदु या उद्देश्य से दूर जाना भी हो सकता है।)

 
 
• **Example:** I apologize for digressing, but could we please go back to the topic at hand? I'm afraid I got sidetracked.
 
 

**Let's see the meanings of the given words**__

 
• To **deviate** means to depart from a norm, standard, or expected course of action or behavior. It can also refer to moving away from a particular direction or goal. (विचलन करने का अर्थ है एक मानक, या कार्रवाई या व्यवहार के अपेक्षित पाठ्यक्रम से हटना। यह किसी विशेष दिशा या लक्ष्य से दूर जाने का भी उल्लेख कर सकता है।)

 
 
• **Example: ***The flight path had to be slightly altered to avoid severe turbulence, causing the plane to **deviate** from its original course.*
 
 
 
• To **come back **means to return or go back to a place, a state, or an activity. (वापस आने का अर्थ है किसी स्थान, राज्य या गतिविधि पर वापस जाना।)
 
 
• **Example:* ****I'm sorry, could you **come back t**o the question I asked earlier? I'm still not clear on your answer.*
 
 
 
• To **remove** means to take away or eliminate something, either physically or figuratively. (हटाने का अर्थ है शारीरिक या लाक्षणिक रूप से किसी चीज़ को दूर करना या हटाना।)
 
 
• **Example: ***The contractor carefully **removed **the old tiles from the floor, making sure not to damage any of the underlying subflooring.*
 
 
 
• To** slow down** means to reduce the speed or pace at which one is moving or working. (धीमा करने का अर्थ है जिस गति से कोई चल रहा है या काम कर रहा है उसे कम करना।)
 
• **Example:** *I know you're eager to finish the project, but you need to **slow down** and double-check your work to avoid mistakes.*

According to the meanings of the given words, *the correct answer is **Option 1, i.e., deviate.***

questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence in which there is an error.**

He did (a)/ not come(b)/ to the meeting, (c)/ didn't he? (d)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. didn't he? .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in part **(d)** of the sentence: "*didn't he?*".
 
• This is a case of a **tag question**, which must match the main statement in terms of tense and meaning.
 
• The main statement uses a negative form: "*He did not come to the meeting*". The tag question should therefore be in the positive form: "*did he?*", not "*didn't he?*".

Correct sentence: *He did not come to the meeting, did he?*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **What is a tag question?**

 
 
• A tag question is a small question added to the end of a sentence to confirm or clarify information.
 
• It typically uses auxiliary verbs and matches the tense and polarity (positive/negative) of the main clause.
 
 
 
• **Rules for tag questions:**

 
 
• If the main clause is positive, the tag is negative.
 
• If the main clause is negative, the tag is positive.

questions.question:
Directions: In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

Good people will make good laws, but good laws passed by a few does not necessarily make a good society.

options.text: Good people will make good laws

questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **A few does not necessarily**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Replace "does not" with "do not" to correct the sentence.
 
• The error here lies in the Subject-Verb agreement.
 
• The basic rule states that a singular subject takes a singular verb while a plural subject takes a plural verb.
 
• "Does" is used after a singular subject.
 
• "Do" is used after a plural subject.
 
• The use of the singular verb form "does" is incorrect in this sentence, as the subject, "good laws" is a plural noun. 
 
• A subject and verb must always be in agreement, meaning the verb needs to be changed to a plural form.
 
• Therefore, "do not" should be used in the given sentence.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2, which contains an error.

Corrected sentence: *Good people will make good laws, but good laws passed by a few **do not **necessarily make a good society.*

questions.question:
Choose the correct option to complete the following sentence :

Our body ___________ balanced diet.
questions.solution:
The correct option to complete the sentence is 1) **needs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence would read: "Our body needs a balanced diet." This is because "needs" is the third person singular present tense of the verb "need," which is appropriate for referring to an ongoing or general requirement or necessity, like the need for a balanced diet.
 
• "Needs" is the third person singular present tense form of the verb "need." This option is used when talking about a requirement or necessity that is ongoing or general, as in this case where the body always requires a balanced diet. So, the sentence "Our body needs a balanced diet" is correct.
 
• The other options do not fit grammatically in this context.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Do need**: "Do need" is an example of emphasis in English. We often use "do" for emphasis in positive sentences, but usually in response to a negative assumption or to contradict someone. In this case, "do need" doesn't fit grammatically because "our body" is a singular subject and "do" is used with plural subjects or the singular pronouns I and you. If you wanted to use emphasis, you would say "does need," as in "Our body does need a balanced diet."
 
• **Needed**: "Needed" is the past tense form of "need." You would use this if the need for a balanced diet was in the past and is no longer true, which doesn't make sense in this context. The need for a balanced diet is an ongoing requirement, not something that only applied in the past.
 
• **Is needing**: This form uses the present continuous tense. In English, we don't generally use the present continuous with stative verbs like "need," which describe states rather than actions or processes. So "Our body is needing a balanced diet" is not grammatically correct. If the need were temporary or happening at this very moment, we might say "Our body is in need of a balanced diet," but generally, we would simply say "Our body needs a balanced diet."

Typically these are categorized into two main types — **infinitive forms **with and without **to* **(e.g., *to go, go*) and **Participle forms** (**-*ing* forms **and **-*ed* forms**) that do not act as the finite verb** **(e.g., *going, gone*). These are also known as **verbals**.

 
 
• For example, ***Jogging **for half an hour daily is good for your health**.*
 
• For example, *I tried to wash my **stained **shirt.*
 
 
 
• The -ed form of participial verbals usually acts as adjectives: **these usually tell us how people *feel* about something or someone**. e.g. shocked, amazed, bored, etc., in contrast to the *-ing* endings which often describe a quality of a person, thing, or idea. e.g., shocking, amazing, boring, etc.
 
• The blank in the given sentence needs an adjective that qualifies the noun 'frown.'
